text:
maria: Heads up — we're seeing repeated oscillation between HPA/VPA/CA in eu-west1 GPU nodepool. External queue metric spikes, HPA scales pods, CA tries to add nodes but node creation fails with egress/IP quota errors and then CA falls back to us-central. Customers see higher tail latency. Anyone digging in?

raj: Yup, got the same alerts. HPA jumped from 8 -> 30 pods in ~2m because redis_queue_depth shot up. CA attempted to provision nodepool-eu-gpu but GCE returned RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED for ephemeral external IPs.

kevin: infra-bot posted the error earlier: `ERROR: quotaExceeded: Quota 'GLOBAL_EXTERNAL_ADDRESSES' exceeded for project` -> node creation aborted.

infra-bot: [automated] Event: failed to create instance: quota error. Attempting fallback to other regions per cluster autoscaler config.

maria: The kicker: VPA recommender had recently bumped pod CPU requests for model-worker -> requests increased, which changes pod packing and HPA sensitivity. VPA updateMode=Auto + short HPA stability window = recipe for thrash.

raj: Our HPA uses an external metric (redis_queue_depth) with a 30s averaging window and no scaleUp stabilization. CA sees pending pods and starts nodes; when nodes fail to launch due to quota, pods stay pending and HPA keeps scaling. Classic positive feedback.

kevin: Two immediate mitigations: 1) add a stabilization window to the HPA + increase metric aggregation (smoother), 2) limit VPA from changing requests until after a canary. Also request quota increase for eu-west1 external IPs.

maria: Agreed. For HPA change, propose:

```
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: model-worker-hpa
spec:
  behavior:
    scaleUp:
      stabilizationWindowSeconds: 120
    scaleDown:
      stabilizationWindowSeconds: 300
  metrics:
  - type: External
    external:
      metricName: redis_queue_depth
      target:
        type: AverageValue
        averageValue: "50"
```

maria: That should stop the 2m rapid spin-up.

raj: For VPA: set updateMode: "Off" for model-worker in prod while we stabilize; switch to recommend-only for now. Also add a resourcePolicy to cap cpu request increases to e.g., +30%.

kevin: I'll file the GCP quota ticket (raising GLOBAL_EXTERNAL_ADDRESSES for eu-west1) and request dedicated reserved IP pool for GPU nodepool to avoid ephemeral exhaustion.

sre-oncall: We should also change CA expander strategy to prefer existing node pools (least-waste) and enable nodePool warmup to reduce cross-region fallbacks. Right now CA expander=anything -> it picks us-central because eu failed.

maria: Cost note: fallback to us-central is causing cross-region egress to our model-serving infra. Preliminary calc: ~3k USD/day extra while this persists. Need to weigh against spinning up reserved GPUs.

raj: Long-term: reserve a small baseline of EU GPU capacity (2-3 nodes) so transient queue spikes don't force cross-region moves. Could be a Dedicated/reserved pool or cheaper preemptible warm pool with taints.

kevin: Action items: 
- kevin -> create GCP quota ticket + reserve IP pool (ETA: 2h)
- raj -> patch HPA stabilization + smoothing, PR up in 30m
- maria -> set VPA updateMode: Off and open infra ticket for VPA policy change (ETA: 1h)
- sre-oncall -> update runbook to include quota check + CA expander config (ETA: today)

maria: Quick debug command if folks want to repro: 
`kubectl get pods --field-selector=status.phase=Pending -n model -o wide`
`kubectl describe pod <pending-pod> -n model`

kevin: Also add a Grafana panel for pending pods per zone + CA activity so we catch cross-zone provisioning earlier.

raj: One more note — the external metric publisher (redis exporter) had a bug and was emitting short spikes when the telemetry exporter restarted. We're patching it to emit 60s rolling average to reduce noise.

maria: OK lets implement the HPA & VPA patches first, then the quota request. I'll open the infra ticket and link PRs. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: [deploy] model-worker-hpa patch deployed to staging (canary)

kevin: good. monitor latency/tokens-per-second and we'll rollback if anything regresses.

sre-oncall: leaving notes in runbook and scheduling a short postmortem for Monday to capture root cause + prevention steps.
